utterances.text: We don't need exact times; nobody knows exact times. We're just trying to get an idea whether it's morning, around noon, afternoon, late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: It certainly wasn't in the morning. It was in the afternoon or around noon, some way into the afternoon, but I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, when you went through Potocari, did you have any trouble driving through the crowd?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: Yes. There were many people there, but the road was free, clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see what was going on in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: Nothing was going on, not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Some people were sitting there, women were there, children. Some were sitting, some were standing, and some were just moving about. At that point in time, nothing -- well, there were many people there. White UNPROFOR vehicles were driving by, our vehicles, our soldiers, their soldiers, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see Muslim civilians being loaded on to buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: Not when I was leaving. On my way back, the buses, yes, I did, on my way back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you see the Muslim men getting separated from their families as they were getting -- as they were getting on the buses?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: No, on my way through I saw a vehicle. There were several buses there. I can't think exactly how many. And people were being loaded. I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At the time did you know who the chief of security for the Bratunac Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade? I know now and I've known for quite some time now. Whether I knew at the time, I don't know. I can't say with precision. I may even not have known or I may have known. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing special really struck you at the time that would cause you to know him or not know him, apparently?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: No. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see any soldiers or officers you recognised in Potocari, either on the way through the first time or as you came back?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: I don't think I saw anyone in Potocari that was familiar on my way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you get any information --

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: On my way back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you have any information that Muslim civilians were being abused and in at least in one case shot and killed right there in front of the Dutch soldiers in Potocari nearby where you were driving, bodies in the woods? Did you get any information about that as an intelligence officer, or as anyone else?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA
utterances.text: No. I did not get that, not even as an intelligence officer. That would have been more interesting to the security service than to my service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise, I have a -- probably another 15 minutes. There's another document or two, so I was hoping to finish today, as I know everyone was. But I will be able to finish up pretty early tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have to stop here. It's 7.00 already. And tomorrow morning we'll sit in the same courtroom at 9.00. Well, Witness, I'm afraid that we have to keep you here overnight because we did not finish your testimony. And during the time you are in The Hague I have to remind you that you are still under oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony today. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, have a good rest. And the hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 7.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of June, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
